analysis.title: SFR REITs: HPA Analysis – October 2026
key_insights: RBC estimates AMH and INVH home portfolio values fell 0.6% and 0.5% month over month in October 2026. That is slightly below September (0.4%-0.5% depreciation) and slightly weaker than October 2024/2025 (0.3%-0.5% decline).
RBC calls the October decline consistent with the fall seasonal weakness of recent years. It says higher mortgage rates have not hurt prices dramatically to date.
Nearly all SFR focus markets depreciated in October. South Florida was the only market with sequential appreciation (+0.2% in the INVH portfolio). Seattle was the weakest at -1.3% in both portfolios.
Spread between the weakest and strongest appreciating SFR markets was 150 bps in October, slightly wider breadth than in September.

AMH trades at an implied 33% discount to RBC's estimated home portfolio value. The discount is 34% including the value of its development business, at 1.5x book value for land/CIP ($911 million at 9/30/26).
INVH trades at a 36% discount to RBC's estimated portfolio value. The discount is 0-1% wider month over month, reflecting portfolio depreciation and roughly flat equity performance.
RBC values the AMH home portfolio at $26.3 billion ($27.6 billion including cash/JVs/land/CIP), 78% above the 9/30/26 book value of $14.8 billion.
RBC values the INVH home portfolio at $36.6 billion ($37.7 billion including cash/JVs/fees/land/CIP), 59% above the 9/30/26 book value of $22.9 billion.
AMH's 3Q26 reported gain on sale implied 25% appreciation, behind 2Q26 and below RBC's estimate. AMH includes impairments in its gain on sale figure.
INVH's 3Q26 reported gain on sales implies 148% appreciation on houses sold, well above 2Q26 and above RBC's estimate.
Cost savings from development give AMH higher appreciation versus book value than INVH.
Weakest AMH markets in October: Seattle (-1.3%), Charlotte (-0.7%), San Antonio (-0.7%). No AMH focus market appreciated.
Weakest INVH markets in October: Seattle (-1.3%), Denver (-0.9%), Carolinas (-0.7%).
RBC argues underlying home value should be the floor value for SFH businesses. Its assumptions give no value for scale, operating platform, ancillary services or AMH development expertise.

market_movers.rationale: Price target is the average of NAV ($44/sh), DCF ($32/sh) and 16.0x FFO ($33/sh). The stock trades at a 33-34% discount to RBC's estimated home value.
Price target is the average of NAV ($38/sh), DCF ($23/sh) and 13.5x FFO ($27/sh). The stock trades at a 36% discount to RBC's estimated home value.

sector_views.rationale: RBC rates AMH Outperform and INVH Sector Perform. Both trade at wide discounts to estimated portfolio value. October depreciation was seasonal.

earnings_insights: AMH 3Q26 reported gain on sale implied 25% appreciation on homes sold, below the 2Q26 reported gain and below RBC's estimate. AMH includes impairments in its gain on sale figure.
INVH 3Q26 reported gain on sales implies 148% appreciation on homes sold, well above 2Q26 and above RBC's estimate.

macro_indicators.indicator: US home prices (Zillow, SFR focus markets)
macro_indicators.reading: AMH portfolio -0.6% MoM, INVH portfolio -0.5% MoM (RBC estimates)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Seasonal fall weakness, not outside typical patterns. RBC says higher mortgage rates have not dramatically affected prices to date.

risk_factors: Economic trends: employment and wage growth, household formation and relative housing affordability.
Supply: AMH has seen significant competing supply in some markets.
Move-outs to buy a home: if tenants start buying homes again, the affordability tailwind for SFR rents could reverse.
Development risk: AMH is a significant developer, which brings execution risk.
INVH: more competitive for-sale housing, excess build-to-rent supply in some markets, and earnings volatility from the ResiBuilt homebuilding ramp.
Regulatory: the SFR industry has faced greater regulatory scrutiny.
